LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 LISTENING COMPREHENSION: SELECTIVE LISTENING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What can you do to ensure you capture relevant information from a speaker?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. distinguish between specific and general information from a listening text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. select specific information from a listening text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. listen and respond to texts on leadership,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. emphasise the value of listening skills in communication.  Listen to an audio text and decide whether the information presented is specific or general. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views.  Search online for audio recordings on leadership and attentively listen to text for specific information. Adjust light intensity when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties.  Watch a role play and respond to questions. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing. E. and answer questions posed by the speaker.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical Thinking is developed as the learner listens and selects general and specific information from oral texts.

Values:
 Integrity is promoted as the learner nurtures discipline while listening to texts on good governance.

 Social justice is enhanced as the learner learns the need for fairness while listening to oral texts on leadership.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

 Good governance is enhanced as the learner listens to texts on leadership.

 Effective communication is achieved as the learner listens and responds to audio texts on good governance.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates selective listening to their learning in Kiswahili.
